hero.title: ResuHost Resume API
paragraphs: ResuHost is a FastAPI-powered backend system for managing resume data and generating polished, print-ready PDF resumes using server-side HTML templating and WeasyPrint rendering.

Built as a personal tool to solve a real problem — keeping resume content consistent across applications — the project grew into a full REST API with AI-assisted tailoring, Docker deployment, and support for both local and cloud-hosted Postgres databases.

features.text: Full CRUD Across Seven Resource Types

concepts.label: KEY CONCEPTS LEARNED
items: Structuring a FastAPI project with layered routers, schemas, and service modules for long-term maintainability.
Using SQLAlchemy ORM with Pydantic for validated, type-safe database interactions.
Rendering server-side HTML templates with Jinja2 and converting them to PDFs with WeasyPrint.
Designing a RESTful API surface that cleanly separates resource concerns across endpoints.
Integrating a locally-hosted LLM (Ollama) to intelligently rewrite resume content for specific job descriptions.
Containerising a multi-service app with Docker Compose, supporting both local Postgres and Supabase cloud.
Writing health check and debugging endpoints to support rapid local development.

body.title: Why I Built This
paragraphs: Tailoring a resume for each job application is repetitive work — the content is largely the same, but bullets need rewording and sections need reordering. ResuHost started as a way to centralise all of my resume data in a structured database so that any version of my resume could be generated on demand rather than maintained as separate documents.

The project became a meaningful technical exercise in API design, templating, and containerisation. Building something I actually use day-to-day meant the requirements were grounded in real friction rather than hypothetical needs.

body.title: API Design & Architecture
paragraphs: The API is organised around seven resource categories: work experience, education, projects, activities, skills, resume snapshots, and a health endpoint. Each resource has its own router and schema definitions, keeping the codebase modular and easy to extend.

Pydantic models handle all request and response validation, while SQLAlchemy manages the ORM layer against a PostgreSQL database. The project supports both a locally-running Postgres instance and Supabase as a cloud-hosted alternative, controlled entirely through environment variables.

body.title: PDF Generation Pipeline
paragraphs: Generating a resume PDF involves rendering a Jinja2 HTML template populated with data fetched from the database, then passing the rendered HTML to WeasyPrint for conversion to a styled PDF document. Templates are kept separate from business logic, making it straightforward to swap in different resume layouts or styles without touching the API code.
This approach keeps PDF output deterministic and fully server-side — no browser dependencies, no headless Chromium, just a clean Python pipeline from data to document.

body.title: AI-Assisted Tailoring with Ollama
paragraphs: One of the more interesting features is the integration with Ollama, which allows the API to rewrite resume bullet points to better match a provided job description. The endpoint accepts raw bullet text and a job posting excerpt, sends a structured prompt to a locally-hosted language model, and returns a set of rewritten alternatives.

Running Ollama locally keeps the feature self-contained with no external API costs or data privacy concerns. The integration is modular enough to swap the model or move to a hosted provider without touching the rest of the API.
